title: Domain registry (skills/domains.json)
description: The buyer-facing category domains skills/ is organized into. Each domain is a top-level folder under skills/ and accepts one or more technical skill-id prefixes, either directly (`prefixes`) or split into named subcategories (`subcategories`), one folder level deeper, for a domain broad enough to need it. This is the single source of truth scripts/validate.js and scripts/lib/skills.js use to check a skill lives under the right domain/subcategory — it is also meant to be read by anything presenting the catalog to a non-technical audience (docs, the installer app).

id.description: Folder name under skills/, e.g. 'sales'. English, so it reads the same in every market.

name.description: Buyer-facing category label in English, e.g. 'Sales & Presales'.

description.description: One plain-language sentence: what this domain is for, in terms a non-technical buyer recognizes.

prefixes.description: Technical skill-id prefixes (without the trailing '-') this domain accepts directly, e.g. ['av']. Mutually exclusive with 'subcategories' — a domain either holds skills directly or splits into subcategories, not both.

subcategories.description: One extra folder level under this domain (skills/<domain>/<subcategory>/<skill-name>/), for a domain broad enough that buyers still benefit from a finer split (e.g. Development -> SEO / Code / UX-UI).
